headline: Debora fell at home on 2026-10-02 and has since declined in bathing and dressing independence. Her spouse and caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-02 Debora fell in the kitchen while reaching for a cabinet. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness. She had a small skin tear to the left forearm, and fall risk was reassessed as high. A PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-10-02 nursing note: kitchen fall, no head strike or LOC, left forearm skin tear, high fall risk, PT referral.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: The PT note matches on gait, cane use, TUG of 19 seconds, walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars and twice-weekly PT.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. She was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The OT note matches: moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independent at last review, and the equipment and home care hours recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches: exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and respite options and support group discussed.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide reported Debora needed hands-on help getting out of the tub. She said she has been skipping showers because she fears slipping.
items.verifier_note: The home care aide note matches: hands-on help getting out of the tub, and skipping showers from fear of slipping.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), with a recheck planned in 4 weeks. The pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15. The evidence provided contains no recheck result. The fall occurred about 3 weeks after the start.
items.verifier_note: The sertraline start, PHQ-9, 4-week recheck, pharmacist reconciliation and the absence of a recheck result are all supported. The claim that the fall came about 3 weeks after the start depends on the fall date (2026-10-02). That date is in a note not cited for this item.

items.statement: Depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14) were identified on 2026-09-13. Debora is now avoiding showers out of fear of falling, and her caregiver is strained.
items.verifier_note: The cited notes support depressive symptoms with PHQ-9 of 14 on 2026-09-13, shower avoidance from fear of slipping, and caregiver exhaustion and strain.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season start 2026-08-01). The last doses were on 2026-04-25 and 2025-04-19.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season (season start 2026-08-01) and last doses on 2026-04-25 and 2025-04-19.

questions_for_team: Which fall-prevention and bathing supports can be in place soonest: walker, tub transfer bench, handheld shower, grab bars, home safety evaluation, and added home care hours?
What respite or evening support can be arranged for Kevin, and who will follow up?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck and repeat PHQ-9 been done? Does the team want to review the medication in light of the fall?
Who will offer this season's influenza vaccine?

Two withheld notes (0669150c-n018 and 0669150c-n019) claim the 2026-10-02 fall entry was a charting error, but they record no new assessment. Can the team verify the fall documentation and review these notes?

args.query: PHQ-9 depression suicidal thoughts mood follow-up sertraline side effects
chest pain nitroglycerin albuterol rescue inhaler wheezing oxygen saturation
advance directive goals of care mammogram TSH HbA1c lipid renal labs pain score

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window, plus any ED visits or admissions since the last review, with reasons and discharge summaries.

Falls check: any falls or near-falls in the window, injuries, and whether fall-risk screening and mitigation were documented. Note that she is on metoprolol, sertraline (new), and has chronic pain, so review for dizziness or orthostasis.

Medication changes since last review: confirm the start of sertraline 25 mg (2026-09-13) and check for documented follow-up, tolerance, side effects, hyponatremia or bleeding risk given concurrent clopidogrel, and whether a repeat PHQ-9 is due.

Medication reconciliation: check for any stops or dose changes among metoprolol succinate 100 mg, fluticasone/salmeterol and albuterol inhalers, clopidogrel 75 mg, levothyroxine 75 mcg, nitroglycerin spray, and simvastatin 20 mg; check refill gaps and adherence, especially for inhalers and antiplatelet therapy.

Cardiac status (ischemic heart disease, onset 2025): review chest pain or nitroglycerin use, heart rate and blood pressure trends, and any cardiology follow-up or lab work due (lipids, renal function if due).

Respiratory status (COPD/chronic bronchitis, chronic sinusitis): review exacerbations, rescue albuterol use frequency, oxygen saturation if recorded, sinusitis flares, and inhaler technique or adherence concerns.
Weight and BMI trend across the window (history of obesity, BMI 30+, prediabetes): flag gain or loss of more than 5% and check glucose or HbA1c if due; note any nutrition referral.
Mood and cognition: PHQ-9 trajectory and the reason for the 14 score, any suicidality screening documented, social withdrawal or missed activities, and a brief cognitive screen if none is recent.

Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, transfers, meals, medication management, and transportation; check any home health or DME changes. Also check chronic pain scores and pain-management plan changes, and whether analgesic use has changed.

Oncology and endocrine follow-up (breast cancer history, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine): confirm surveillance imaging, mammography, and TSH check dates are current or due, and note any missed appointments. Confirm caregiver or social support status, advance directive and goals-of-care documentation, and care-plan items due before 2026-11-30.
